sample.cause: Poor hot-air weld quality at coved wall-to-floor transition, mechanical damage during installation of grow racks, or chemical attack from sanitiser
sample.hazard: Bund membrane weld failure allowing nutrient solution to escape to subfloor
sample.mitigation: Specify 100% vacuum-box weld testing of all bund seams at commissioning, install redundant conductive leak-detection tape under the membrane, and require quarterly visual bund inspection in service manual
sample.consequence: Up to 600 litres of nutrient solution leak to the marine plywood and steel cross-members, causing hidden corrosion, biological contamination, and eventual structural compromise of the container floor
sample.existingControls: Coved 150 mm upstand membrane, leak-detection sensor in low point of bund reporting via controls and Internet-of-Things gateway, captive bund sized to full reservoir volume

sample.cause: Aluminium Z-purlins and steel corner-post fixings penetrate the polyurethane foam layer, creating cold spots below dewpoint at high internal relative humidity
sample.hazard: Thermal bridging at structural fixings causing internal condensation and mould
sample.mitigation: Add thermal break pads (polyamide or high-density polyethylene) at every steel-to-steel fixing penetration and verify with thermographic survey during factory acceptance test
sample.consequence: Persistent condensation behind fibre-reinforced plastic lining promotes mould growth, fails United Kingdom Regulation (European Community) 852/2004 food hygiene audit, and degrades insulation effectiveness
sample.existingControls: Closed-cell foam sprayed continuously over purlins, fibre-reinforced plastic lining sealed with silicone, climate control unit holds relative humidity 65-75%

sample.cause: Substrate contamination at spray application, thermal cycling between United Kingdom winter and internal grow-room temperatures, or substandard foam chemistry
sample.hazard: Polyurethane foam delamination or long-term shrinkage creating uninsulated voids
sample.mitigation: Require pull-off adhesion testing on witness panels at factory, specify minimum 35 kilograms per cubic metre core density, and include energy-trend alerting in farm-management dashboard to detect insulation degradation early
sample.consequence: Effective wall U-value drifts upward over 5-10 years, heating, ventilation and air-conditioning load increases, daily energy consumption exceeds 250 kilowatt-hours per day target, and operating economics break
sample.existingControls: Specification of closed-cell foam to BS 5241, qualified spray-applicator subcontractor, energy metering telemetry from power distribution flags drift

sample.cause: Ultraviolet exposure, thermal cycling, or vibration during road transport degrading ethylene propylene diene monomer gaskets at cable, drain, and condenser-line glands
sample.hazard: Penetration gland degradation compromising ingress protection and allowing pest entry
sample.mitigation: Specify ethylene propylene diene monomer gaskets with verified 10-year ultraviolet rating, fit external drip-shields over all roof penetrations, and add gland-integrity check to commissioning and annual service checklist
sample.consequence: Loss of EN 60529 ingress protection rating, ingress of rodents or insects compromising food safety and hygiene certification, water ingress damaging electrical distribution
sample.existingControls: IP65-rated gland selection, stainless cover plates, annual planned-maintenance inspection in service manual

sample.cause: Polypropylene creep under sustained load and warm humid environment, or insufficient mid-span support spacing
sample.hazard: Channel sag or warping causing nutrient solution pooling and uneven flow
sample.mitigation: Specify glass-filled polypropylene channels for tiers carrying heaviest crops and add a creep-deflection acceptance test at six-month and twelve-month service intervals
sample.consequence: Localised root anoxia, dead plant sites, reduced yield, and unscheduled rack downtime for channel replacement
sample.existingControls: Mid-span support every 1.0 metre, 1.5 percent fall designed in, food-grade polypropylene rated for sustained 40 degrees Celsius

sample.cause: Dissimilar-metal contact wetted by nutrient solution splash and high relative humidity
sample.hazard: Galvanic corrosion at aluminium frame to stainless fastener interfaces
sample.mitigation: Insert nylon or ethylene propylene diene monomer isolating washers at every aluminium-stainless interface and require an annual torque-check service procedure documented in the operations manual
sample.consequence: Loss of fastener pre-load, frame loosening, potential rack instability and channel misalignment
sample.existingControls: Anodised aluminium extrusions and stainless 304 fasteners specified

sample.cause: Resonant excitation during flatbed haulage on a partially loaded container with no internal damping
sample.hazard: Rack rocking or fastener loosening under road-transport vibration
sample.mitigation: Add nylon-insert lock nuts on all primary structural fasteners and require a documented post-delivery torque and alignment check before first water-fill
sample.consequence: Channel misalignment, opened leak paths at drain manifolds, and commissioning delays at customer site
sample.existingControls: Cross-bracing diagonals, rear tie-bars, and bolted connections to floor rails and ceiling Unistrut

sample.cause: Accumulated root mass and microbial biofilm at drain transitions over multiple grow cycles between deep cleans
sample.hazard: Biofilm and root-mat blockage of drain manifolds causing tier overflow
sample.mitigation: Specify clear inspection sections at each tier drain transition and require a weekly visual check plus a quarterly chemical clean-in-place procedure in the operations schedule
sample.consequence: Tier overflow, nutrient solution spill into the container shell bund, lost crop, and unscheduled deep-clean downtime
sample.existingControls: Sloped drain troughs, 32 mm push-fit drain returns at door end, ultraviolet steriliser in nutrient system, and shell bund containment

sample.cause: Inadequate gasket compression, fastener over-torque cracking ceramic, or aperture seal degradation under ultraviolet and thermal cycling
sample.hazard: Water ingress through body seams or apertures wetting internal electronics
sample.mitigation: Specify and verify ingress protection rating IP54 minimum on body and IP65 on apertures by EN 60529 spray and immersion testing on first-article and pre-production samples; add conformal coating on internal printed circuit board assemblies as second line of defence
sample.consequence: Short-circuit of compute or power electronics, premature field failure, warranty returns and reputational damage in premium segment
sample.existingControls: EN 60529 ingress protection rating IP54/IP65 design intent, ethylene propylene diene monomer sealing washers, drainage paths on sensor apertures

sample.cause: Water absorption into glaze micro-cracks or unglazed regions, expansion on freezing, stress concentration at mounting bosses
sample.hazard: Frost-cracking of ceramic body during United Kingdom winter freeze-thaw cycles
sample.mitigation: Run accelerated freeze-thaw test (100 cycles per EN ISO 10545-12) on first-article ceramic bodies; isolate mounting bosses with elastomeric bushings to remove stress concentrations; pre-qualify ceramic supplier with material certificates
sample.consequence: Visible cracking or full body fracture in field, unit must be replaced under warranty, potential safety hazard if unit falls
sample.existingControls: Specification of frost-resistant stoneware with water absorption <0.5 per cent per EN ISO 10545-3, glaze coverage on all external surfaces

sample.cause: Inadequate substrate pre-treatment, edge coverage thin spots, ultraviolet chalking, or salt aerosol exposure in coastal gardens
sample.hazard: Powder coat delamination and substrate corrosion on steel variant
sample.mitigation: Specify minimum 720-hour neutral salt spray test per ISO 9227 on coated samples; require zinc-rich primer plus topcoat (two-coat system) for coastal-grade variant; add edge-radius minimum 1 mm to all formed edges to ensure powder coverage
sample.consequence: Visible rust streaks within two to three years, undermining the 'beautiful in year five' brand promise; structural weakening at fastener points
sample.existingControls: Zinc-phosphate pre-treatment specification, polyester powder coat per BS EN 13438, A4 marine-grade stainless fasteners

sample.cause: Steel body acting as Faraday cage, radome aperture undersized for 868 megahertz long-range radio band, or aluminium sub-frame routed too close to antenna feed
sample.hazard: Radio frequency attenuation or antenna detuning by chassis geometry
sample.mitigation: Run electromagnetic simulation of chassis with antenna placements during industrial design freeze; conduct over-the-air radiated performance testing (total radiated power and total isotropic sensitivity) on first prototype; specify minimum 90 mm radome aperture and 30 mm keep-out from sub-frame to antenna
sample.consequence: Wi-Fi range collapse, long-range mesh unusable between feeders, cellular variant fails to register on network — product non-functional in core use case
sample.existingControls: Non-metallic radome aperture in design intent, lambda/4 antenna spacing target (~86 mm at 868 megahertz), pre-certified radio modules

sample.cause: Solar panel undersized relative to actual neural processing unit and radio duty cycle, combined with several consecutive days of sub-200 watt-hours-per-square-metre irradiance
sample.hazard: Battery undervoltage lockout during prolonged overcast period leaves feeder offline mid-winter
sample.mitigation: Build energy-budget simulation against 10-year United Kingdom Meteorological Office irradiance data for worst-case sites (Glasgow, Manchester) and size panel and battery for 14-day autonomy at 25 per cent duty cycle; implement low-power graceful-degradation mode that disables neural processing unit and falls back to motion-only logging below 30 per cent state-of-charge
sample.consequence: Feeder powers down for days or weeks, missing peak winter bird-activity content, customer perceives product as broken, return rate spikes
sample.existingControls: Brief specifies oversized solar panel; lithium iron phosphate battery management system reports state-of-charge to compute module

sample.cause: Negative temperature coefficient thermistor failure or firmware bug allowing charge current below 0 degrees Celsius cell temperature
sample.hazard: Lithium iron phosphate cell damage from sub-zero charging
sample.mitigation: Hardware-enforced charge inhibit using a dedicated negative temperature coefficient thermistor wired into the charge controller enable pin (not firmware-only); independent firmware temperature check as second layer; environmental chamber qualification at -10 degrees Celsius per IEC 62619
sample.consequence: Lithium plating on anode, capacity loss, internal short circuit risk, potential thermal event — major safety and warranty exposure under IEC 62619 and battery transport regulations
sample.existingControls: Battery management system integrated circuits include temperature monitoring; lithium iron phosphate is the safest commodity chemistry available

sample.cause: Ultraviolet exposure, freeze-thaw cycling, and bird droppings degrading ethylene-vinyl-acetate or ethylene tetrafluoroethylene laminate
sample.hazard: Solar panel output degradation after 3-5 years from encapsulant ageing
sample.mitigation: Specify panels from suppliers with published 25-year power warranty and ultraviolet-A/B accelerated ageing test data; design panel to be field-replaceable as a service part rather than bonded to body
sample.consequence: Watt-peak drops below threshold required for winter operation; product fails the 'beautiful and functional in year five' brand promise
sample.existingControls: Specification calls for ethylene tetrafluoroethylene laminate (more ultraviolet-stable than ethylene-vinyl-acetate); oversized panel provides margin

sample.cause: Nearby lightning strike inducing voltage transient on solar panel cabling, exceeding charge controller absolute maximum input rating
sample.hazard: Lightning-induced surge damages charge controller and downstream electronics
sample.mitigation: Add transient voltage suppressor diode and gas-discharge tube on solar input; route solar cable internally with a small ferrite bead; specification compliance to EN 61000-4-5 surge immunity at 1 kilovolt line-to-ground
sample.consequence: Single-event total product failure requiring full replacement; not covered by typical home insurance for individual feeder
sample.existingControls: None at present in baseline architecture

sample.cause: Vent panel hinge corrosion seizure, paint over-coating during refurbishment, or incorrect set-pressure specification relative to actual cell off-gas reactivity
sample.hazard: Deflagration vent panels fail to open at design pressure during thermal runaway, causing shell rupture and fire propagation
sample.mitigation: Specify vent panels with stainless steel hinges and corrosion-protected set mechanism; size vent area per UL 9540A-validated off-gas reactivity data from chosen cell; mandate annual functional inspection in operations and maintenance manual
sample.consequence: Container shell ruptures explosively, ejecting debris and burning electrolyte up to tens of metres; potential fatality of nearby personnel and total loss of adjacent assets; site insurance claim and regulatory shutdown of fleet
sample.existingControls: Four NFPA 68 / EN 14797 certified vent panels at 50 mbar, tethered, with annual inspection requirement; off-gas detection in fire safety system triggers pre-emptive shutdown

sample.cause: Long-term degradation of polyurethane sealant at dissimilar-metal interfaces, mechanical abrasion at gland plate edges, paint damage during transport and installation
sample.hazard: Corrosion perforation at sealant joints, roof penetrations, and gland plate, allowing water ingress onto live electrical equipment
sample.mitigation: Specify EN 60529 IP66 rating at all penetrations; use EPDM gasket plus secondary silicone bead at gland plate; include 5-year sealant re-inspection and re-application in scheduled maintenance; route condensate drains externally
sample.consequence: Water ingress causes insulation breakdown on direct current busbars or alternating current cabling, leading to ground fault, equipment damage, or arc fault fire; system unavailability and warranty claim
sample.existingControls: ISO 12944 C5-M paint system (240 µm dry film thickness), EN 60529 IP55 door and gland plate seals, weathering steel base material

sample.cause: Mineral wool insulation degradation from coolant leak prior to event, mechanical damage during installation or maintenance, or actual fire load exceeding EN 1363-1 standard test curve
sample.hazard: Fire-rated internal lining fails earlier than 60-minute rating under real thermal runaway fire, breaching fire boundary
sample.mitigation: Commission UL 9540A unit-level fire test on production-representative assembly; specify lining manufacturer with documented post-coolant-exposure fire performance data; install protective steel kick plate at floor level to prevent mechanical damage during racking
sample.consequence: External container surface temperature exceeds threshold for ignition of adjacent assets within National Fire Chiefs Council 3 m separation distance; emergency services unable to safely approach; potential site-wide fire spread
sample.existingControls: EN 13501-1 Class A1 non-combustible mineral wool 50 mm with galvanised steel inner skin facing, EN 1363-1 60-minute rated assembly, fire detection system with early off-gas warning

sample.cause: Under-specified chemical anchor depth for actual concrete pad strength, weld defect at corner casting to underframe interface, or transport tie-down impact loads exceeding casting fatigue limit
sample.hazard: Foundation anchor pull-out or corner casting weld failure under wind, seismic, or transport shock loads
sample.mitigation: Site structural engineer to verify anchor specification against local wind and seismic loads per Eurocode; magnetic particle inspection of all corner casting welds as factory acceptance test; specify transport tie-down points and approved lashing pattern in shipping procedure
sample.consequence: Container shifts on pad during storm or transport incident, shearing alternating current tie-in cables and coolant lines; arc flash, coolant spill, and possible cascading thermal event; commissioning delay and site re-work
sample.existingControls: ISO 1161 corner castings rated for 30,480 kg stacking, M30 grade 8.8 chemical anchors with 200 mm embedment, ISO 1496-1 structural compliance of welded frame

sample.cause: Internal cell defect, overcharge from battery management system fault, mechanical damage during transport, or sustained over-temperature from cooling failure
sample.hazard: Single-cell thermal runaway propagating to adjacent cells and modules, releasing flammable off-gas and igniting a container fire
sample.mitigation: Specify grade A cells with full traceability and matrix testing to UL 9540A at unit and installation level; require module-level off-gas detection with battery management system trip threshold below thermal-runaway onset
sample.consequence: Catastrophic loss of container, possible deflagration event, multi-million-pound site damage, injury or death to nearby personnel, regulatory shutdown of fleet
sample.existingControls: Lithium iron phosphate chemistry (lower runaway risk than nickel-manganese-cobalt), per-cell voltage and temperature monitoring by battery management system, module-level fuses, mica propagation barriers, gas detection feeding the fire detection and suppression system, deflagration vent panel in container roof

sample.cause: Vibration-induced loosening of dripless couplings, gasket degradation from glycol contamination, or freeze damage during winter shutdown
sample.hazard: Coolant leak from cold-plate fitting or hose causing internal flooding and direct-current short-circuit
sample.mitigation: Add redundant leak-detection ribbon at base of every rack with automatic coolant-loop isolation valves; pressure-test entire loop to 1.5 times working pressure during factory acceptance test
sample.consequence: Isolation fault, ground fault current, possible arc event, full system trip, and extended downtime for rack drying or replacement
sample.existingControls: Dripless quick-disconnect couplings, drip trays with leak-detection sensors reporting to controls and supervisory cabinet, isolation monitoring by battery management system

sample.cause: Non-uniform cooling between modules at rack ends versus middle, weak passive balancing current, or inconsistent cell matching at factory
sample.hazard: Cell imbalance and accelerated capacity fade leading to premature end-of-life
sample.mitigation: Specify active balancing at module level (minimum 2 ampere balance current) and computational fluid dynamics validation of coolant manifold flow uniformity to within 5 percent rack-to-rack
sample.consequence: State-of-health falls below 70 percent before contractual cycle count, triggering warranty replacement at substantial cost and potential customer churn
sample.existingControls: Battery management system passive balancing during charge phase, factory cell-grading procedure, cold-plate flow balancing manifold

sample.cause: Thermal cycling, transport vibration over United Kingdom road network, or under-torqued connections at factory
sample.hazard: Busbar or terminal-bolt loosening causing localised resistive heating and possible arc-flash
sample.mitigation: Add fibre-optic temperature monitoring on critical busbar joints feeding battery management system trip logic, and require post-transport torque audit before commissioning
sample.consequence: Hot spot ignition source, module-level fire, and direct-current arc that may breach module casing and trigger thermal runaway
sample.existingControls: Calibrated torque assembly with witness-marking, Belleville washers on busbar bolts, infrared inspection during commissioning

scores.summary: Register shows competent mechanical-engineering detail but is heavily skewed toward S3 structural/envelope risks, residuals collapse uniformly to S2L1/S3L1 suggesting systematic optimism bias, ownership is almost entirely 'Mechanical lead' with no commercial or regulatory roles visible, and programme-level risks (cost overrun, regulatory, supply chain, market) appear absent from the sampled rows.
scores.nextFix: Force a second pass that (a) adds at least one S4-S5 row for electrical arc-flash or CO2 asphyxiation in a sealed container, (b) requires residual likelihood to stay ≥2 for any risk whose mitigation is 'inspect' or 'specify', and (c) mandates distinct owners across Electrical, Controls/IoT, Commercial, and Regulatory disciplines before the register is accepted at gate review.

scores.summary: Register is entirely empty — zero rows submitted, so no quality can be assessed on any dimension.
scores.nextFix: Populate the register with at minimum 15–20 risks spanning hardware failure modes (IMU drift, ferrule wear, battery thermal runaway, cellular module RF certification), programme risks (single-supplier CF shaft, UKCA/MDR regulatory denial, launch window slip, cost overrun), and safety/liability risks (fall-detection false negative causing delayed emergency response, capacitive sensor skin-contact allergy), then resubmit for scoring.

scores.summary: Technically detailed and well-specified on engineering hazards but the visible sample is severity-4-heavy with no spread below 3, residuals collapse uniformly to S3L1 or S2L2, and programme/commercial risks (cost overrun, regulatory, supplier, launch window) are absent from the sample entirely.
scores.nextFix: Add at least 6 programme-level rows covering: (1) single-source ceramic supplier failure, (2) UKCA/radio type-approval denial slipping launch, (3) BOM cost overrun vs. premium price-point, (4) ML model accuracy below marketable threshold at DVT, (5) battery UN38.3 / UKCA certification timeline, (6) retail channel window miss — then re-score severity across all 28 rows to produce a genuine 1–5 distribution rather than a 3–4 cluster.

scores.summary: Strong technical FMEA depth with specific mitigations and credible residuals, but the visible sample is dominated by severity 4-5 hardware hazards with no programme, commercial, or regulatory risks in sight, severely limiting its utility for go/no-go gates and insurer conversations.
scores.nextFix: Add at minimum six programme-level rows covering: single-cell-supplier qualification failure, G99 DNO approval delay past commissioning window, capital cost overrun breaching the £180k target, key-person dependency on battery safety lead, export/import tariff shock on LFP cells, and UL 9540A test failure requiring redesign — then re-score severity distribution across all 32 rows to confirm spread from 2 to 5.
